newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Thursday, issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and they are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.
Traders said the rates moved in a narrow range in slow trading today, with no market-moving news in prospect.
Many investors were sidelined, waiting for a cut in bank reserve ratio, they said. The People's Bank of China in early July promised there would be such a cut this year.
"There will be no big changes either in rates or volumes in the foreseeable future before the reserve ratio cut," said one trader.
"Lenders and borrowers have struck a new balance after sharp falls in late August triggered by the interest rate cut by the central bank," he added.
The People's Bank of China cut interest rates for bank deposits and loans respectively by an average of 1.5 and 1.2 percentage points on August 23.
Traders said state-run banks had sufficient funds after the interst rate cut and lent out money on the market.
"State-run banks kept on lending," said a second trader.
Short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank, have been net borrowers recently, traders said.
